# Information Architecture

## Definition

Information Architecture is the structuring of information — its meaning, organisation, classification and relationships — so that people and processes can find, understand and use it consistently.

## Explanation

Information architecture concentrates on the upper and middle [[Architecture Layer|layers]]: which information the organisation needs, how it is classified ([[Taxonomy]]), how it is represented as an [[Information Model]], and how it relates to business processes. It consumes meaning from the [[Semantic Model]] and hands representation choices to the [[Logical Data Model]].

## Distinctions

- Compared with [[Data Architecture]]: information architecture is more concerned with meaning, structure and use; data architecture additionally addresses realization, integration, storage and operations.
- In user-experience design, "information architecture" also denotes navigation and content structure of websites. That usage is out of scope here.

## Examples

- A classification scheme for product documents used by several departments.
- An information model of "Case", "Party" and "Decision" for a public-sector organisation.

## Open Questions

- Different frameworks draw the boundary with data architecture differently; flagged, not resolved.
